name: cardiac investigations overview
title: Investigating suspected ischemic heart disease decision chart: the pretest probability picks the test, from no testing in asymptomatic low-risk patients, to CT coronary angiography as a test of exclusion, to exercise or pharmacologic stress testing at intermediate probability, to coronary angiography after a high-risk result; for chambers, valves and left ventricular function the gold-standard imaging test is chosen by the structure

root.title: Suspected ischemic heart disease: WHICH TEST? Match it to the PRETEST PROBABILITY and the QUESTION
lines: history + exam are the most important tests · pretest probability: age, male sex, the type of chest pain, risk factors
a NORMAL ECG does NOT exclude ischemia · chest pain is the LAST step of the ischemic cascade, after perfusion, wall motion and ECG change

groups.title: INTERMEDIATE (25–75%): a STRESS test
lines: can they WALK on a treadmill, and is the resting ECG normal?

head: h
NO testing
false positives harm: anxiety, insurance, further tests
watch: New atypical pain or risk factors

head: h
CT coronary angiogram (CTCA)
a test of EXCLUSION: negative predictive value 99%
use: beta blocker 1 h before: slows the heart, less motion

head: h
Exercise stress ECG
simple, inexpensive
read: exercise < 6 min = the strongest prognostic sign
watch: • uncontrolled HF or arrhythmia, PE, dissection

head: h
Stress IMAGING
nuclear perfusion (MPI) or stress echo
use: more accurate than the ECG alone
watch: • stress echo: none, but body habitus limits it

head: h
DRUG stress imaging
orthopedic, vascular, neuropathy, rate-slowing drugs
use: PREFERRED for stress echo · or caffeine in the last 12 h
read: Rest vs stress, as for any MPI
watch: sustained VT, recent MI, severe hypertension

head: h
Coronary angiogram
GOLD standard for coronary anatomy; treat it at once (PCI)
read: A tight lesion does NOT prove the pain is ischemic
watch: • vascular injury commonest · contrast kidney injury

head: h
Chambers, valves, LV function
start with chest X-ray + transthoracic echo (TTE)
use: • valves: ECHO (TEE if TTE falls short)
watch: normal > 50% · prognosis falls < 30–35% · echo or MUGA
